title: Spatiotemporal clonal architecture of the newborn mouse forebrain.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded GSE341480_p4_forebrain_lineage_metadata.rds (14 MB) from GEO and read it in R: 416,390 cells x 14 columns, no missing values; clone_index (measured lentiviral barcode), injection_date (8 levels, E11-P0), mouse (27), region (5 dissected regions), cell-type labels at 4 resolutions. 288,826 distinct clone strings, 229,065 singletons, 59,761 clones with 2+ cells covering 187,325 cells; 9,835 of those clones span more than one region; 71,004 cells carry multiple barcodes joined by ';'; no clone string occurs in two mice. Dispersed-clone rate by class: inhibitory neurons 0.388, excitatory neurons 0.055, microglia 0.504. Leave-one-mouse-out baseline on the 9 mice with 4+ regions (149,251 cells): AUC (area under the ROC curve) 0.607 from clone size alone, 0.723 from clone size plus cell subtype. HEAD on the count matrix: 5,053,499,513 bytes (RDS). UCSC Cell Browser JSON lists counts_matrix.mtx.gz at 6,221,133,717 bytes, 416,390 cells; MERFISH (spatial imaging) sub-dataset 9,271,988 cells, 500 genes, no clone column.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Paper full text is paywalled and not in Europe PMC; I read only the abstract, the GEO series summary and the Cell Browser description (29,779 genes, 10x v3.1, FACS-sorted GFP+ cells). Gene expression values were not opened (matrix is over 50 MB). The Cell Browser text says ~8.2 million MERFISH cells, but its JSON lists 9,271,988.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO GSE341480 is public with no login; I downloaded the metadata file. The count matrix is on GEO (5.05 GB RDS) and on UCSC Cell Browser (6.2 GB mtx.gz); checked by HEAD request only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Clone identity (clone_index) is a column. The proposed 'clone spans more than one region' label takes one groupby of clone_index x region inside the same table, with no cross-source join; I computed it in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are per-cell UMI (unique molecular identifier) counts over 29,779 genes, deposited in full, not referenced. Seen only as file listings and sizes, not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: Values are raw 10x UMI counts, the standard unit; metadata holds counts and categories, with no mixed units. Matrix values themselves were not inspected.

a5_enough_rows.note: 187,325 cells in 59,761 clones of 2+ cells (verified). The independent unit for a held-out split is the mouse: 27 in total, 9 with 4+ regions sampled.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2 GB after streaming the 6.2 GB mtx.gz and keeping ~2,000 genes for 187k cells
a6_fits_laptop.note: Borderline. The 5 GB RDS would need about 15-25 GB of RAM in R (estimate). The Cell Browser mtx.gz can be streamed line by line with a gene filter. The baseline needs no GPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 416,390 cells matches the stated ~416,000. 93 sample IDs x 2 libraries matches GEO's 186 samples. The MERFISH count (9.27M vs ~8.2M) disagrees, but that data is not used.

a8_label_provenance.note: Clone barcodes are measured by targeted PCR of viral barcodes, and region comes from manual dissection; neither is a model output. Cell-type columns come from clustering the expression, so they must not be used as targets.

B1.why: Metadata RDS plus a separate 5-6 GB matrix, joined on cell barcode rownames; the join was not run.

B2.why: Metadata is an R RDS (needs R); the matrix comes as RDS or mtx.gz. The metadata parsed first try.

B3.why: One platform (10x v3.1), one lab, one protocol across all 93 libraries (from description and metadata).

B4.why: No censored values, but dispersal is only observable in mice where several regions were dissected (verified: 9 of 27 have 4+).

B5.why: 71,004 cells carry multiple barcodes joined by ';', so clone calling is ambiguous and a merge rule is needed (verified).

B6.why: Column names are self-explanatory, but there is no data dictionary and the methods are paywalled.

C1.why: Whether expression adds to the 0.723 metadata AUC is informative either way, but it is confounded by clone size.

C2.why: No predictive model of clone dispersal found; clone2vec (open) is exploratory and was not applied to this data.

C3.why: Unique-application angle: turn the paper's descriptive dispersal finding into a held-out-mouse prediction test.

C4.why: Lineage barcoding needs in-utero viral injection and extra sequencing; predicting from expression alone would remove that step.

C5.why: I computed a dummy baseline: clone size plus subtype gives 0.723 AUC leave-one-mouse-out.

D1.why: Geneformer and scGPT (single-cell foundation models) have open weights; both are human-trained, so mouse genes need ortholog mapping.

D2.why: Frozen embeddings are possible, but 187k cells on a CPU is several hours (estimate). PCA features are a cheap alternative.

D3.why: Geneformer is Apache-2.0 and scGPT is MIT (from general knowledge, not rechecked); GEO data is open.

E1.why: Leave-one-mouse-out split; no clone string appears in two mice (verified).

E2.why: 9 mice with 4+ regions, each holding thousands of clone cells (verified).

E3.why: Per-subtype dispersal rate and clone-size-only logistic regression, computed: AUC 0.607 and 0.723.

E4.why: No replicate clones. The 0.504 dispersal rate in microglia, which are not born from these progenitors, hints at a barcode noise floor.

E5.why: Inhibitory clones disperse far more than excitatory ones (0.388 vs 0.055, verified), matching the abstract.

E6.why: Labels can be shuffled within mouse, and clone size can be ablated against the expression features.

E7.why: Earlier STICR atlas GSE188528 from the same lab (65,700 cells on Cell Browser) is a second lineage dataset; not opened.

E8.why: The paper reports enrichments, not a predictive number; the full text was not retrieved.

G1.why: Gene symbols, probably Ensembl IDs in the features file (not opened); no other standard IDs for cells.

G2.why: SFARI Gene, a curated autism gene list, joined on gene symbol; the abstract says dispersed clones are enriched for such genes.

G3.why: Gene-level join is one-to-one after resolving symbols.

G4.why: Asks whether disorder-risk genes predict dispersal, but the paper already reports the enrichment.

H1.why: Both local and dispersed clones are present: 9,835 of 59,761 multi-cell clones are dispersed (verified).

H2.why: One lab, one mouse strain, one collection age (P4, postnatal day 4).

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, scoped to sampled regions and FACS-captured cells.

H4.why: The sampling limits (which regions were dissected per mouse) show in the metadata, not in any open text.

I1.why: Nowakowski lab and developmental neurobiology lineage groups; no named user who needs a predictor.

I2.why: A good predictor could flag dispersing lineages in unbarcoded atlases; modest change to experiments.

I3.why: AUC for dispersed vs local is roughly aligned; there is no explicit decision threshold.

I4.why: Metadata lookup already reaches 0.723 AUC; expression may add little beyond cell subtype.

J1.why: Grouped CV, foundation-model embeddings, confound control (clone size), external lineage dataset.

J2.why: Neurodevelopment cell types are interpretable, but barcode artefacts need expert judgement.

J3.why: The clean clone/dispersal table and the metadata baseline are useful on their own.

J4.why: No budget written yet; about 2 weeks is plausible.

existing_models.name: clone2vec (Kharchenko lab, bioRxiv 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Exploratory clone embeddings; benchmarked on synthetic sparse sampling and several lineage datasets (embryonic CNS, blood, cancer); no held-out predictive score of dispersal; not applied to STICR data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Depends on barcode induction timing; exploratory and not causal; they point to CoSpar for fate-bias questions.

backbone.name: Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome foundation model; human-trained, mouse genes mapped to human orthologs) or scGPT
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop, several hours to embed ~187k cells (estimate); PCA on 2,000 genes as a cheap alternative
backbone.licence: Geneformer Apache-2.0, scGPT MIT (not rechecked); GEO data public

integration.partner_dataset: SFARI Gene autism risk list; earlier STICR atlas GSE188528 (Bandler et al. 2021) for external validation
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the genes that predict whether a GABAergic lineage disperses across forebrain regions overlap with neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes beyond what cell subtype explains?

controls.positive_control: Inhibitory-neuron clones disperse more than excitatory ones (0.388 vs 0.055 verified); the model must recover this. Trivial target: predict dissected region from expression.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle dispersal labels within mouse and within size bin; the model should fall to about 0.5 AUC beyond the size-only baseline (0.607).
controls.external_validation: Leave-one-mouse-out within GSE341480; then test on GSE188528, an earlier STICR atlas from the same lab (not opened).

honest_claim_h3: Among virally barcoded, FACS-captured cells from P4 mice in which several forebrain regions were dissected, the model predicts whether a cell's sampled clone was observed in more than one region, beyond what clone size and cell subtype already explain.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a single newborn-mouse brain cell's gene expression to predict whether its sister cells migrated to other brain regions.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene expression of each cell plus its clone's size: 187,325 cells in 59,761 barcoded clones (149,251 cells from the 9 mice with 4+ regions sampled).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the cell's clone (cells sharing an inherited viral DNA barcode, read by sequencing) was found in more than one hand-dissected forebrain region.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Developmental neurobiologists could infer migratory lineages in atlases that have no barcodes. If expression adds nothing beyond cell subtype, that shows dispersal is set by cell class alone.

pitch.headline: 416,390 newborn-mouse forebrain cells with measured clone barcodes across 5 regions and 8 labelling days, fully public on GEO.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: 59,761 multi-cell clones, 9,835 of them seen in several regions, all from 27 mice with no clone shared between animals (verified). Earlier atlases focused on the cortex.
pitch.the_win: Beat the 0.723 leave-one-mouse-out AUC that clone size plus cell subtype already reach, using expression alone, then confirm it on the 2021 STICR atlas.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A clean clone-dispersal table plus a finding that cell subtype alone explains dispersal, which itself bounds how much the expression state encodes migration.
pitch.who_wants_it: Nowakowski lab and lineage-tracing groups deciding whether barcoding is needed to study interneuron dispersal.

ml_idea: Per-cell binary classifier (dispersed vs local clone) on PCA or frozen Geneformer embeddings plus log clone size, with leave-one-mouse-out CV on the 9 multi-region mice. Compare against the size+subtype logistic baseline (0.723 AUC), then transfer to GSE188528.

effort.compute_note: Metadata baseline timed in practice (under 1 minute in R). Matrix streaming, embedding throughput (~15 cells/s CPU) and RAM are estimates; the 6.2 GB matrix was not downloaded.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Stream ~2,000 genes and fit expression PCA plus size within inhibitory neurons only, leave-one-mouse-out. If AUC does not beat size+subtype (0.723 overall) by about 0.03, stop.

verdict_reason: Open, measured clone labels with real counts. But model-readiness is 7/12 (6 GB matrix, multi-barcode ambiguity, sampling-dependent label), and cell subtype already gives 0.723 AUC, so expression may add little.
